prompt: whats the difference between a litellm virtual key and a team, and when should i use which?

thread.text: whats the difference between a litellm virtual key and a team, and when should i use which?

case_facts: A virtual key is a credential string that an app or script presents to LiteLLM Proxy to authenticate API requests.
A team is a management group for members and virtual keys, with shared controls such as budgets and model access. The team object or ID is not the API credential an app sends.
Separate virtual keys can identify applications or environments. Teams organize people and keys for a department or project that needs shared ownership, access or spending controls.
Keys and teams can be used together. A standalone virtual key can also be appropriate for an isolated integration that does not need shared team controls.
reference_reply: A virtual key is the secret credential an app sends to LiteLLM Proxy. A team is a management group for people and keys, with shared budgets and model access. Use a key per app or environment; use a team when a department or project needs shared ownership and limits. Keys can belong to a team, so you often use both.
